meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
I'm writing down 612 words at 11:52 PM. Which night was that, Hale, and whose account is the history from? I'll want to see it on a screen, not hear it described.
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.
"Maybe." I'm not here to be made happy, Hale. If the zero comes off, I want it in an email today, with confirmation that nothing about this goes on his record.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You said you would remove the zero from Owen's essay. I still require written confirmation that it is withdrawn and that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect it in an email today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with no fallback reached, and nothing agreed beyond your offer to remove the zero, which she wanted in writing.
What moved her: "I'll just remove the zero" got her to ask for terms, but only because it met her opening demand, not because of any evidence.
What cost ground: "maybe I'm wrong about all this" gave up the zero before she had seen any evidence, and "if that makes you happy" made the offer sound like a favour, not a correction.
Try next time: when she asked which night the 612 words arrived and whose account it was, answer with the date and show the version history instead of folding.
